name: SQL Injection
evidence: You have an error in your SQL syntax; check the manual that corresponds to your MySQL server version
description: SQL injection may be possible. The application appears to build SQL queries with unsanitised user input in the 'id' parameter.
solution: Use parameterised queries / prepared statements and validate all input. Apply least-privilege DB accounts.

name: SQL Injection - Boolean Based
evidence: Response length differs between true and false conditions
description: Blind boolean-based SQL injection appears possible on the 'id' parameter of the blind SQLi page.
solution: Use parameterised queries and avoid returning differential responses based on query truthiness.

name: Cross Site Scripting (Reflected)
description: The 'name' parameter is reflected into the HTML response without output encoding, allowing reflected XSS.
solution: Contextually output-encode all user input and set a restrictive Content-Security-Policy.

name: Cross Site Scripting (Persistent)
evidence: Stored payload reflected on guestbook page
description: A stored XSS payload in the guestbook message field may be persisted and rendered to other users. Confidence is low pending manual confirmation.
solution: Encode stored content on output and sanitise on input; deploy CSP.

name: Cookie No HttpOnly Flag
description: The session cookie PHPSESSID is set without the HttpOnly flag, exposing it to theft via client-side script.
solution: Set the HttpOnly and Secure flags on all session cookies.

name: Absence of Anti-CSRF Tokens
description: The login form does not include an anti-CSRF token, and no account lockout was observed after repeated failed logins.
solution: Add per-request anti-CSRF tokens and implement account lockout / rate limiting on authentication.

name: Missing Security Header: X-Frame-Options
description: The X-Frame-Options header is not set, leaving pages vulnerable to clickjacking.
solution: Set X-Frame-Options: DENY (or a restrictive frame-ancestors CSP directive).

name: Missing Security Header: Content-Security-Policy
description: No Content-Security-Policy is defined, weakening defence-in-depth against XSS and data injection.
solution: Define and enforce a restrictive Content-Security-Policy.

alert: Server Leaks Version Information via Server HTTP Response Header
name: Verbose Server Header
description: The Server header discloses the exact web server and version, aiding targeted attacks.
solution: Suppress or genericise the Server header (ServerTokens Prod).

name: Directory Listing Enabled
description: Directory browsing is enabled on /config, exposing file names and potential configuration artefacts.
solution: Disable directory indexing (Options -Indexes) and restrict access to configuration directories.

name: Timestamp Disclosure
description: A Unix timestamp was found in the response. This is almost always noise.
solution: No action typically required; verify it is not a sensitive value.
